claims.claim: A complete commercial kitchen build-out for a typical (~1,000 sq ft) kitchen runs on the order of $250,000-$500,000 in construction, or $400,000-$700,000+ with equipment.
claims.episode_span: A typical restaurant kitchen build-out lands between three hundred thousand and six hundred thousand dollars before the first plate leaves the pass.
claims.source_title: Commercial Kitchen Construction Cost: 2026 Guide - Modular Culinaire
claims.supporting_quote: For a 1,000 square foot kitchen (the industry average), that translates to: Construction costs alone: $250,000–$500,000 With equipment added: $400,000–$700,000+

claims.claim: Commercial kitchen construction typically costs $250-$500 per square foot (up to $600 in the most expensive cities).
claims.episode_span: Square-foot costs of three to six hundred dollars therefore persist across independent restaurants
claims.source_title: Commercial Kitchen Construction Cost: 2026 Guide - Modular Culinaire
claims.supporting_quote: commercial kitchen construction typically runs $250 to $500 per square foot for a complete buildout.

claims.claim: The U.S. Food Code is an FDA model from which health jurisdictions nationwide develop their own retail food-service sanitation standards, and which version is in force varies by health jurisdiction -- there is no single national retail food code.
claims.episode_span: Jurisdictional fragmentation remains the largest policy obstacle, because even a technically superior module still faces dozens of separate approval processes
claims.supporting_quote: The U.S. Food Code is released by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a guide or model from which health jurisdictions nationwide can develop their sanitation standards for food service and retail.

claims.claim: Ventilation control and fire protection of commercial cooking operations (hoods, ducts, suppression) are governed by a dedicated standard, NFPA 96.
claims.episode_span: no redesign can eliminate the need for listed suppression systems or reliable temperature control
claims.source_title: NFPA 96, Standard for Ventilation Control and Fire Protection of Commercial Cooking Operations
claims.supporting_quote: NFPA 96, Standard for Ventilation Control and Fire Protection of Commercial Cooking Operations

claims.claim: In commercial kitchens the exhaust hood is typically combined with a fire-suppression system so that grease-fire fumes are vented and the fire is extinguished quickly -- the hood/suppression pair is one integrated safety assembly.
claims.episode_span: utility-core modules that already contain hood, fire suppression, make-up air, and electrical distribution in a single tested package
claims.supporting_quote: In commercial kitchens exhaust hoods are often used in combination with fire suppression devices so that fumes from a grease fire are properly vented and the fire is put out quickly.

claims.claim: The all-in cost to open a restaurant runs roughly $100 to $800 per square foot, with a median of about $450 per square foot (whole-restaurant figure, not kitchen-only).
claims.episode_span: Square-foot costs of three to six hundred dollars therefore persist across independent restaurants
claims.source_title: How Much Does It Cost to Open a Restaurant? - Toast
